context:
Goal: end the arbitrary lengths on your typed override and on an Opus ask (your ruling R12).
Problem (rule): a one-act override ends after 10 minutes and a plain Opus ask after 2 hours; both numbers were lane or coordinator picks, never your words.
Based on (ruling): R12, your words "opus 4h etc also feels super arbitrary".
Departs from: main ends them at 10 minutes and 2 hours — they end on use, on an off command, or at your next typed message.
home: lane owner-override-one-route (your typed override goes through one route)

options.gain: No made-up minutes; each lasts as long as you meant.
options.how: A one-act override ends when it is used, when you type `override off`, or at your next typed message; an Opus ask with no length lasts until the session ends or you type `opus off`.
options.label: End on use or your word (Recommended)
options.lose: An Opus ask you forget about runs to the session's end.

options.gain: The simplest rule, and nothing outlives your next word.
options.how: A one-act override and an Opus ask both end at your next typed message.
options.label: Both end at your next message
options.lose: A long Opus job needs the ask again after each message you type.

options.how: Keep both numbers, now as your ruling.
options.label: Keep 10 minutes and 2 hours

reply: Filed: a one-act override ends when used, on `override off`, or at your next typed message; an Opus ask with no length lasts until the session ends or `opus off`. Lane owner-override-one-route builds it.
short: Override and Opus: when they end
title: When your override and an Opus ask end, with no fixed minutes
why: Your R12 ruling asks for no arbitrary lengths; these two need your word on what ends them.
